label: Thomas Aquinas, In octo libros Physicorum…: If a moving thing lacks an internal source of motion…
locator: VII, lect. 1 n. 885: its principle of motion is from without
interpretation: Aquinas' exposition of Physics VII.1, 241b24-27: if a thing does not have in itself the principle of its motion but has it from without, as in things moved by compulsion, it is clearly moved by another; the doubtful case is a mobile with an internal principle. Read as the same proposition as Aristotle's claim ARIST-PHYS-241B24-NO-INTERNAL-OTHER-MOVER-A. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
